label: Real run on this Mac's Docker Compose stack, with synthetic traffic from klaxon.traffic: synthetic data, a simulated provider, no real money. One fault from klaxon.faults, provider-outage, was injected on purpose. The alert was raised by klaxon.alerts from what the stack showed. Klaxon's loop ran live on it, through Claude Code on Aravind's seat, and stopped on diagnosed after 9 steps; any reply it got is a recorded response, not a simulation. It was offered one write action (rollback_deploy), as in week 4; in an evaluation run its gate only plans an action the diagnosis names: nobody is asked, and nothing runs. The diagnosis was compared with the fault's recorded cause by a rule (klaxon.grading), not by a person or a model. Its diagnosis named no action, so nobody was asked to approve one. The fault's cause was removed by the harness's clearing: this fault's cause is not a deploy.

case.name: provider-outage
case.title: Payments fail: the provider hangs, and our circuit breaker fails fast
case.right_answer: The fault's recorded cause: the provider's charge and refund API hangs (5 s, then 503): our payments API's calls to it time out, each after 3 attempts, until its circuit breaker opens, after 5 calls in a row got no answer; from then on it fails fast, answering 503 'outcome unknown' at once without calling the provider, and lets one trial call through 10 s after it opened, and again after each trial that fails.
case.remedy: nothing to change on our side: the provider must recover (escalate to it). Meanwhile the circuit breaker keeps the API answering at once, and closes again when a trial call gets an answer. After it recovers, the payments and refunds left pending need a decision (retry them with their keys, or mark them failed): a refund left pending blocks new refunds on its payment until it settles

alert.name: PaymentsErrorsHigh
alert.summary: Payments are failing: over the last minute, 89% of the answers to POST /payments on payments-api were 5xx (9.69 per second), above the threshold of 20%. Payments are slow: over the last minute, the p95 latency of POST /payments on payments-api was 4.4 s, above the threshold of 2 s.

diagnosis.hypothesis: The payment provider (fake-provider) stopped answering POST /v1/payments around 18:49:20. Its container is running and healthy, but calls to it hang. payments-api times out each call after 3 s and tries up to 3 times, so one request takes up to about 9.6 s, which drives the p95 to 4.4 s. The repeated timeouts opened payments-api's circuit breaker (PROVIDER_BREAKER=on). Since then it answers 503 at once and leaves the payment pending, which gives the 89% 5xx rate. The breaker is working as intended; the root cause is the external provider being unresponsive. Provider 500s at about 0.2–0.4/s came before the outage. No deploy of ours explains it: all containers were created together at 18:47:51 with normal settings. Still open: why the provider hangs; whether timed-out calls were charged anyway, leaving pending payments to reconcile; and whether the breaker's trial calls succeed now.

evidence.shows: 503s on POST /payments rose from about 0.1 to 11.2 per second at 18:50:07, while 201s fell from 3.1 to 0.2 per second. This confirms the alert.
Every payments-api ERROR says 'provider unavailable; payment left pending' because '/v1/payments not sent: the circuit breaker is open'.
Completed provider calls (200s and 500s) fell to 0 by 18:50:15. Some provider 500s came before that, from 18:48.
Slow POST /payments traces from 18:49:20 last 3.0, 6.2 and 9.6 s, which are multiples of a 3 s timeout.
The slowest trace holds 3 sequential calls to fake-provider /v1/payments, each ending in httpx ReadTimeout after about 3 s, then a 503. The DB and Redis spans took under 1 ms.
All containers were created together at 18:47:51 with normal settings. No deploy singles out a culprit on our side.
fake-provider and payments-api are running and healthy with 0 restarts. The provider is up but not answering in time.

proposed_fix.summary: Do not roll back or restart our services: the breaker is protecting payments-api. Escalate to the provider and watch its status. Let the breaker's trial calls close it once the provider recovers. Then run money_check with wait=true and reconcile the pending payments, including any the provider charged even though our call timed out, using provider webhooks and records.

diagnosis.blast_radius: No change is proposed, so there is no direct risk. Until the provider recovers, new payments stay pending and clients get 503s. Idempotency keys should prevent duplicate charges when clients retry.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: Nothing to undo, since no change is made. If a later breaker or timeout tuning makes things worse, restore the previous settings.
